q: can I give Motrin to my 8 month old for fever
text: Yes, you can give ibuprofen (Motrin) to an 8-month-old for fever: acetaminophen (Tylenol) and ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin) help reduce fever in children, according to MedlinePlus [6]. Do not use ibuprofen in children younger than 6 months [6]. Know your child's weight before giving it, and give it every 6 to 8 hours [6]. The dose depends on the child's weight — check the packaging or leaflet to make sure the medicine is suitable, or speak to a pharmacist or doctor if you are not sure [3]. You can also give paracetamol instead; both work similarly, at the dose your paediatrician recommends, every 6 to 8 hours [5]. Keep breastfeeding or offering plenty of fluids, and do not undress or sponge your child down to cool them [3][2]. Get medical advice if you are worried, or if the medicine is not helping [3].

q: my son threw up twice this morning, what should I give him to drink
text:
Give small sips of an oral rehydration solution, according to the SEUP. When he vomits, wait 20 minutes, then give 2–5 ml of oral rehydration solution every 5 minutes for an hour [3]. If he keeps it down, you can slowly give it more often [3]. Do not use homemade solutions or commercial soft drinks [3]. Oral rehydration solutions for children can be bought without a prescription [5].

Watch for signs that he is getting worse: vomiting a lot, not keeping down solids or liquids, or vomiting even when he takes nothing; green vomit, blood, or vomit that looks like coffee grounds; or being sleepy, limp, very thirsty, with sunken eyes, crying without tears, or urinating little [7]. If any of these appear, he needs to be seen in the emergency department [7].

q: how do I know if my child is getting dehydrated from vomiting
text:
Dehydration happens when the body loses more fluid than it takes in, and vomiting is one of the causes [1]. The main risk of vomiting is dehydration, according to the SEUP [3].

What to do: give oral rehydration fluids. After your child vomits, wait 20 minutes, then give 2–5 ml of oral rehydration solution every 5 minutes for an hour [5]. If they keep it down, you can slowly increase how often you give it [5]. Don't use homemade solutions or fizzy drinks [5]. Oral rehydration fluids from a pharmacy are the most helpful for mild dehydration, and sports drinks without caffeine can also help [2].

Get help if your child is very drowsy, vomits many times, or won't take fluids — check with your doctor [3]. If you think they are severely dehydrated, call your doctor [2].

q: my 5 year old has been coughing all night, what can I do
text:
A cough that keeps a child awake at night is common in viral colds and in asthma, where the cough often comes at night [5]. If your child has asthma, the cough and any wheeze usually improve with a bronchodilator such as salbutamol, according to the SEUP [2]; the dose is the one your doctor or the inhaler leaflet gives.

Things that can set it off include colds, allergy, pollution or exercise, and in preschool children viral respiratory infections are the main cause of wheezing [2]. Avoiding the triggers can ease symptoms, according to the WHO [6].

Get medical care if your child has a lot of trouble breathing, continuous coughing, difficulty speaking, or a bluish colour around the lips, which means the oxygen in the blood is low [5].

q: my son has been coughing for a week after a cold
text: A cough that lingers after a cold is common, and some symptoms of a cold can last for 10 to 14 days, according to MedlinePlus [6]. If the cough comes in bouts that are worse at night, or your son makes a "whoop" sound when gasping between coughs, it may be whooping cough: after about a week of cold-like symptoms, coughing bouts that last for a few minutes and are worse at night can appear, and the cough may last for several weeks or months [4]. Whooping cough can be serious, and it is important for babies and children to be vaccinated against it [4]. Ask for an urgent appointment with your doctor if you think your child may have croup — a barking cough that sounds like a seal, often worse at night — or if your child is getting worse or not getting better [3].

q: he has a cough but no fever and is eating normally
text: A cough without a fever, with normal eating, is usually caused by a common infection of the airways, and fever is the body's natural response to fighting infections like coughs and colds, according to the NHS [1]. Keep offering fluids and let him rest; there is no need to treat a fever that is not there, and medicines for fever are only for when a child actually has a fever and is uncomfortable [5]. If he is eating and drinking normally, that is reassuring. See your doctor if he stops wanting to eat, is not his usual self and you are worried, or has a fever that lasts 5 days or more [1].

q: my daughter has red spots all over her stomach and they appeared today
text: A rash of red spots that came on today is common in children, and most rashes can be cared for at home [5]. Raised, itchy spots or patches may be hives, which can usually be treated at home [5]. Chickenpox spots can appear anywhere on the body and be red, pink, darker or the same colour as the surrounding skin [4]. If it is chickenpox, give plenty of fluids, paracetamol for pain, cut the fingernails and put socks on their hands at night to stop scratching, and use cooling creams or gels [1]. Do not give ibuprofen unless a doctor tells you to, as it may cause serious skin infections, and do not give aspirin to children under 16 [1]. Call your local emergency number if there is swelling around your child's mouth or they are struggling to breathe [5].

q: my 2 year old has little red bumps on his legs and keeps scratching them
text:
Little itchy red bumps on the legs are often hives, a raised, itchy rash that can come in different shapes and sizes [1]. Hives are common in children and are not usually serious.

For the itching, ask a pharmacist about antihistamine treatment — but tell them your child's age, because this treatment may not be suitable for young children [7]. Keep your child's nails short and try to stop them scratching, since scratching can make the skin redder and itchier [4].

Get help straight away if your child's lips, mouth, throat or tongue suddenly swell, if they are breathing fast or struggling to breathe, if their throat feels tight or they struggle to swallow, if their skin, tongue or lips turn blue, grey or pale, or if they become limp, floppy or not responding like normal — these can be signs of a serious allergic reaction [7].

q: these spots dont seem to bother her but there are more every morning
text: Spots that don't bother her and keep increasing each morning are common in nappy rash, which can usually be treated at home, according to the NHS [2]. Nappy rash can look like red or raw patches on the bottom or the whole nappy area, or spots, pimples or blisters that may be red or brown [2]. Keep the area clean and dry, change nappies often, and use a barrier cream at each change [2]. If the spots are on the face, inside the elbows, behind the knees, or on the hands and feet, and the skin is dry and itchy, this may be eczema, which is not contagious and is common in babies and children, according to MedlinePlus [6]. Eczema is treated with skin creams, medicines, light therapy and good skin care, and you can help by avoiding irritants like certain soaps, fabrics and lotions [6]. See your doctor if the rash spreads, blisters, or the skin becomes raw or painful [2].

q: my 6 year old fell from the bed and hit the back of his head
text:
Most head injuries in children are not serious, and most children recover quickly [2][6]. For the headache, you can give ibuprofen or paracetamol at the dose your doctor indicates [6]. Let him rest, avoiding sport and screens for 24 to 48 hours, then return gradually to normal activities [4]. He can eat and drink as usual, and he can sleep — for a more significant knock, it is worth waking him every 4 hours [6].

Watch over the next 24 hours for a severe or worsening headache, repeated vomiting, confusion or disorientation, behaviour changes, trouble speaking or walking, or blood or clear fluid from the nose or ears [4]. Get urgent medical help if he was knocked out, cannot stay awake, has a seizure, is vomiting or dizzy, or fell from more than 1 metre [2][5].

q: what foods should I start with for a baby who just turned 6 months
text:
Around 6 months, milk alone no longer meets your baby's energy and nutrient needs, so solid foods are needed as well, according to the WHO [1]. Start with small amounts and increase them gradually as your baby grows, and build up the number of meals to 2–3 a day between 6 and 8 months [1]. Keep breastfeeding (or formula) going alongside the food [1][2].

At the beginning, how much your baby eats matters less than getting them used to eating, and they will still get most of their energy and nutrients from milk, the NHS says [2]. Offer a variety of foods, and increase the amount and variety gradually until they can eat the same foods as the rest of the family in smaller portions [2].

Give one new food at a time so you can spot any allergic reaction, such as a rash, diarrhoea or vomiting, MedlinePlus advises [3]. Do not give honey before the age of one, and avoid cow's milk before one year [3].

q: how much water can a 9 month old drink
text: For a 9-month-old, breast milk or formula stays the main drink, and it should be offered on demand rather than in set amounts, according to the AEP [2]. If your baby has at least 4–5 breastfeeds a day, no other milk is needed [2]. Water comes with meals and is not measured out: the AEP says caregivers offer healthy food and the baby decides how much to eat or drink, so there is no fixed quantity to aim for [6]. During illness, the WHO says to increase fluids, including more frequent breastfeeding, and to offer soft, favourite foods [1]. Never add salt to what you give, and keep salt under 1 g a day before 12 months [3]. If you are worried your baby is drinking too little or too much, ask your doctor.

q: my baby refuses vegetables but eats fruit all day
text: It is common for babies to prefer fruit, and the AEP says you can keep offering a wide variety of fruits and vegetables at any daily meal, changing how you serve them — puréed, mashed or in small pieces [2]. Offer vegetables again and again alongside fruit; early exposure to different tastes, including bitter ones like some vegetables, makes children more likely to eat them later [2]. Keep giving whole fruit rather than juice, since juice offers no nutritional benefit over whole fruit and can displace other foods [2]. If your baby is under a year, avoid green leafy vegetables such as chard, spinach and borage because of the nitrate risk [2].

q: my daughter is 13 months and still mostly drinks formula
text: At 13 months, formula is no longer needed — your daughter can drink pasteurised whole cows' milk as her main drink, according to the NHS [6]. She should be eating 3 meals a day with a variety of foods, plus 2 healthy snacks between meals [6]. Offer starchy foods like potatoes, bread and rice; fruit and vegetables; full-fat dairy such as cheese and yoghurt; and protein from meat, fish, eggs, dhal, beans, chickpeas or lentils [6]. Good snack ideas are soft ripe fruit, cooked or raw vegetable sticks, plain unsweetened full-fat yoghurt, cheese sticks, toast fingers, or unsalted rice cakes [6]. Keep giving full-fat dairy, as children under 2 need the vitamins and extra energy in it [6]. If she was born prematurely, ask your health care provider for advice on feeding [3].

q: how often should a newborn poop
text:
How often a newborn poops varies from baby to baby — the rhythm and consistency of stools differ between people, according to the SEUP [3]. It is not essential that a baby has a bowel movement every day [3]. What matters more is hard, dry stools or pain when passing them: constipation is stools that are too hard, with discomfort or incomplete emptying, sometimes with fewer bowel movements [6].

For a baby under 6 months, keep the usual feeding — breast milk or formula [3]. Do not give laxatives or enemas without asking your doctor [3].

See your doctor if there is blood in the stool, a lot of tummy pain, or the baby is very floppy and crying a lot, or vomiting many times and unable to keep down solids or liquids [3].

q: my 9 month old suddenly wakes up every two hours at night
text: It is common and normal for a 9-month-old to wake at night: night wakings are physiological, and almost 30% of children still wake at night at one year, according to the PUC Chile manual [2]. Babies this age often need to fall back to sleep on their own, and if they always fall asleep in your arms they will want the same to get back to sleep [2]. Try to let them settle themselves rather than stepping in each time, so a sleep habit does not form [2]. If your child seems unwell, fever and lack of sleep can trigger some night-time waking episodes [1].

q: my 4 year old wakes up coughing only when he lies down
text:
A cough that comes on when a child lies down is a common symptom of asthma in children, according to MedlinePlus: coughing, especially at night or early morning, is one of its signs [4]. Other signs can include chest tightness, wheezing (a whistling sound when breathing out), shortness of breath, feeling tired or irritable, and trouble eating [4]. These symptoms can be mild or severe and may happen often or only once in a while [4].

Keep the room free of smoke and ventilated, and offer plenty of fluids [5]. For a young child, saline nose drops before sleep can help [5]. Do not give cough syrups or other cold medicines, especially under 6 years [5].

Get medical help right away if there is severe coughing, serious breathing problems, or the face, lips or fingernails turn very pale or blue [4].

q: my son has asthma and is using albuterol more than usual
text: A flare-up of asthma is when the usual symptoms — cough, wheeze, chest tightness — get worse than normal, according to MedlinePlus [4]. Most flare-ups are mild and can be treated at home with bronchodilators like salbutamol, and symptoms usually settle within a few days, though they can last up to a week, according to the SEUP [3]. Give salbutamol through a spacer device, with a mask for small children, never straight into the mouth — it works less well that way [3][5]. If there is no clear improvement, go to a health centre [5]. Get urgent help if he is very restless or drowsy, turns blue or pale, breathes faster and faster, his ribs or chest pull in, or he needs inhalations every two hours or less [5].

q: she is making a strange noise when she breathes but is still smiling
text: A strange noise when breathing can be croup, an inflammation of the vocal cords and windpipe that often starts like a cold and causes a barking cough, a hoarse voice and high-pitched sounds when breathing, according to MedlinePlus [3]. It is usually caused by a virus, is more common in children between six months and three years, and most viral cases are mild and can be treated at home [3]. Symptoms generally get worse at night and last three to five days [3]. If you are worried about your child's breathing, call your doctor straight away [3].

q: my 6 year old says his chest hurts when he takes a deep breath
text:
Chest pain when breathing deeply can be a sign of asthma, according to the WHO: asthma symptoms include chest tightness that makes it hard to breathe deeply, and they are often worse at night or with exercise [1]. If your child has a cough, fast breathing, or you can see the ribs pulling in or the chest sinking with each breath, that is difficulty breathing and needs urgent care, according to the SEUP [2][5]. q: my baby had a seizure last year and has a fever today
text:
A febrile seizure can happen when a child has a high temperature, and it is not usually serious, according to the NHS [3]. It can seem frightening, but it is unlikely to harm your child or cause long-term effects [3].

If your baby has another seizure now: do not move them or try to hold them in place, do not put anything in their mouth, and do not try to lower their temperature by undressing them or sponging them with cold water [5]. Put them in the recovery position once the seizure stops [5].

Get medical help if your child has a seizure [3]. Call your local emergency number if a seizure lasts more than 5 minutes, if they have trouble breathing, if the stiffness and twitching is on only one side, if they are more sleepy than usual for more than 1 hour afterwards, or if they have more than one seizure within 24 hours [2].

q: my 4 year old had a seizure when he was a baby, does that change anything now
text:
A febrile seizure can happen when a child has a high temperature, and it is not usually serious or likely to cause long-term effects, according to the NHS [2]. Having had one as a baby does not mean you can prevent them: you cannot prevent febrile seizures, and they are not the same thing as epilepsy, though children who have had one have a slightly increased chance of epilepsy later in life, which is rare [3].

If your child ever has a seizure, keep them safe while you wait for medical help: check the time it starts and ends, protect their head with your hands or something soft, and remove nearby dangerous objects [4]. Do not move them or hold them in place, and do not put anything in their mouth [1]. After it ends, put them in the recovery position [4].

Get medical help if your child has a seizure, and call your local emergency number if it lasts more than 5 minutes, they have trouble breathing, or they are more sleepy than usual for over an hour afterwards [5].

q: my child has a sore throat and white stuff on the tonsils
text:
A sore throat with white patches on the tonsils can be tonsillitis, an infection of the tonsils that is a common childhood illness, according to the NHS [1]. The tonsils look red and swollen, and some children get pus-filled spots or white patches on them, along with problems swallowing, a high temperature, coughing, a headache, earache or feeling sick [1].

For comfort, have them drink plenty of water, eat cool or soft foods, suck on ice cubes or ice lollies, and rest; do not give young children anything small and hard to suck because of the risk of choking, and children should not gargle with salt water [6]. A pharmacist can suggest treatments such as lozenges or throat sprays [2].

See a doctor if the symptoms do not go away within a week, or if your child keeps getting throat infections [2]. Get help right away if your child has pus-filled spots on the tonsils or a sore throat so painful it is difficult to eat or drink [2].

q: when should I take my kid to the doctor for a sore throat
text:
A sore throat is usually caused by a virus, like a cold or flu, and normally gets better by itself within a week, according to the NHS [3][5]. For comfort, offer plenty of water, cool or soft foods, and rest; children should not gargle with salt water or suck anything small and hard because of the choking risk [5]. Paracetamol or ibuprofen can help the pain — ask a pharmacist about these and about lozenges or sprays [6]. Children should not take aspirin [1].

See a doctor if your child is under 5 and needs help for a sore throat, or if it does not improve after a week [2]. Get urgent help now if your child has trouble breathing or cannot swallow, is drooling, makes a high-pitched sound when breathing, or has severe symptoms getting worse quickly [2].

q: my son has been scratching his scalp and has white flakes
text:
White flakes on the scalp with itching are most often dandruff, a common skin condition that is not harmful and cannot be caught, according to the NHS [6]. It is not caused by poor hygiene, though it can be more obvious if the hair is not washed regularly [1].

Wash the hair regularly with a gentle shampoo, and see a doctor if things do not get better in a month [1]. If the flakes are greasy or yellowish and form a crust, this may be cradle cap, which is harmless and usually goes away on its own within a few months [4]. Cradle cap is not itchy or painful and does not bother the child [3].

If the scalp is red, scaly and itchy, or there is patchy hair loss, a doctor can check whether it is another skin condition such as eczema or ringworm [1].

q: my daughter has a tick attached to her leg
text:
A tick attached to the skin should be removed carefully, according to the NHS. Use fine-tipped tweezers or a tick-removal tool, grasp the tick as close to the skin as possible, and slowly pull upwards, taking care not to squeeze it or leave any mouthparts in the skin [6]. Then clean the bite with antiseptic or soap and water [6].

Keep the tick if you can, and note where on the body it was attached and about how long it was there — your doctor will want to know this if your daughter becomes unwell [1]. Watch for early signs of Lyme disease over the following days and weeks: an expanding rash at the bite site (sometimes target-shaped), fever, chills, fatigue, headache, swollen lymph nodes, or muscle and joint aches [2]. See your doctor right away if she was bitten by a tick and develops these symptoms [1].

q: my 3 year old was stung by a bee on the hand
text:
A bee sting on the hand is usually a mild allergic reaction, and most children get only pain, redness and swelling where they were stung [2]. If there is a stinger left in the skin, scrape it out sideways with a fingernail or the edge of a card, then wash the area with soap and water and put a cold pack on it for a few minutes to ease the pain and swelling [2].

Watch your child closely for the first minutes to hours, because a severe allergic reaction called anaphylaxis can start very quickly and can be life-threatening [1]. Signs to look for include itching or hives, swelling of the eyelids, lips, tongue or ears, intense generalised redness, sneezing, difficulty breathing, dizziness, loss of consciousness or vomiting [4]. If any of these appear, use an adrenaline auto-injector if one is available, injecting it firmly into the outer thigh at a 90-degree angle and holding it for 10 seconds, and get emergency help at once [4].

q: my child put a coin in his mouth but I got it out
text:
Small objects like coins can block the airway and cause choking, and young children are most at risk, according to MedlinePlus [1]. Keep small objects out of reach and supervise your child while he eats [1].

If he is conscious, can breathe, talk or cry, and his lips are a good colour, sit him upright and encourage him to keep coughing, according to the Hospital Niño Jesús [2]. Watch for signs of trouble breathing or swallowing, ongoing gagging, persistent cough, hoarseness or drooling [2].

If instead the cough is weak or absent, he cannot breathe, talk or cry, or turns blue, ask for help and look in his mouth, removing the object only if you can see and reach it [2]. For babies under 1 year, give 5 back blows and 5 chest thrusts; for children over 1 year, use the Heimlich manoeuvre, repeating until the object comes out or he becomes unconscious [3].

q: my baby has a temperature of 100.4, is that considered a fever
text:
100.4 °F = 38 °C.

If your baby is under 3 months old, a temperature of 38C (100.4 °F) (100.4F) or higher needs a doctor the same day [5].

For an older baby, yes — 100.4F (38C (100.4 °F)) is considered a fever, according to the NHS [1][3]. A normal temperature in babies is about 36.4C (97.5 °F), but it varies from child to child [3]. Fever is not an illness itself; it is usually a sign the body is fighting an infection [6].

You can usually care for them at home, and the temperature should come down over 1 to 4 days [2]. Give plenty of fluids — if your baby is breastfed, keep breastfeeding as normal — and check on them regularly, including during the night [2]. If they are distressed or uncomfortable, you can give paracetamol or ibuprofen, checking the packaging or leaflet that the medicine suits your child [2]. The dose depends on their age and weight, so follow the leaflet or ask a pharmacist or doctor [2].

Get medical advice if you are worried, or if the medicine is not helping [2].

q: she was outside all day and now has a headache and feels weak
text:
Most headaches are not serious and go away on their own, according to the NHS [5]. Being outside all day can leave her short of fluids, and not drinking enough fluids is a common cause of headache [4].

What to do now: have her drink plenty of water and get plenty of rest [5]. If she also has a cold or flu, that can make a headache worse, so let her relax — stress makes headaches worse too [5]. You can give paracetamol or ibuprofen for the pain [5]; the dose depends on her weight, and PediBot's dose calculator covers those two medicines.

Get medical help if the headache is very intense and does not respond to the usual treatment or keeps getting worse, if she sleeps much more than usual or is hard to wake, or if she has other neurological symptoms such as not seeing well, not moving an arm or leg properly, or difficulty walking or speaking, according to the SEUP [2].

q: my son has been throwing up after being in the sun
text:
Heatstroke is a serious condition that can affect children, especially in hot weather, and nausea or vomiting is one of its symptoms, according to the SEUP [4]. It happens when the body cannot control its temperature, often after long time in the sun, intense activity in hot weather, not drinking enough, or wearing clothes that stop sweating [4].

While you get help, move your child out of the sun into a cool place and give small sips of water or squash if they can keep fluids down [5]. Do not give them anything to eat if they are being sick, and do not give them paracetamol without checking the leaflet first [5].

Get help now if your child is confused or not responding as usual, has a stiff neck, a sudden severe headache, blue, grey or pale skin, or is having severe difficulty breathing [7].

If your child is under 3 months old, a fever needs a doctor the same day.

q: how many wet diapers should a 4 month old have
text:
A 4-month-old should wet diapers frequently, with clear, odourless urine — especially if they are breastfed only [4]. A baby who has not wet a diaper for 3 hours or more is a sign of dehydration [1][3].

Keep offering breast milk or formula on demand; if your baby has diarrhoea or vomiting, they lose water and salts and can become dehydrated quickly [2][6].

See a doctor as soon as possible if your baby has any fever, diarrhoea lasting more than a day, frequent loose stools or vomiting, or signs of dehydration such as fewer wet diapers, no tears when crying, a dry mouth, or unusual sleepiness or irritability [3].

q: can babies get dehydrated from breastfeeding
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Signs of dehydration: sunken eyes, little urine, dry mouth, persistent vomiting or heavy diarrhoea >24 h
text:
Breastfeeding does not cause dehydration — it protects against it. The WHO lists exclusive breastfeeding for the first six months as a key measure to prevent diarrhoeal illness, and says breastfeeding should continue during episodes of diarrhoea [5]. The SEUP agrees: keep breastfeeding normally, and even more often if the baby wants it [3].

If your baby is losing fluids from vomiting or diarrhoea, the priority is replacing them. The SEUP advises waiting 20 minutes after a vomit, then giving oral rehydration solution, 2–5 ml every 5 minutes for an hour, and increasing the frequency if it is well tolerated [6]. Do not use homemade solutions or commercial soft drinks [6]. Oral rehydration solution is absorbed in the gut and replaces the water and electrolytes lost [5].

If your baby is severely dehydrated, fluids may need to be given through a vein in hospital [2].

q: should I give my daughter the HPV vaccine
text:
The HPV vaccine protects against human papillomavirus, a common virus spread through skin contact, usually during sex. Some types are linked to cervical, mouth, anal, penile, vulval and vaginal cancer, and genital warts [1]. It works very well: since it has been used, there has been a big drop in young people getting conditions linked to HPV, such as cervical cancer and genital warts [2].

In the United States, the ages and doses for the HPV vaccine follow the national immunization schedule, so ask your doctor when your daughter is due. The most common side effects are mild and do not last long: swelling or pain where the injection was given, headache, a high temperature, dizziness, feeling sick, tiredness. Severe allergic reactions are very rare, and the person who vaccinates her is trained to treat them immediately [5].

Heavy periods are common in teenagers in the first years after menstruation starts, and are usually due to a temporary immaturity of the hormone axis rather than disease, according to Ecimed [4]. A swollen eyelid when your child wakes up can be an early sign of roseola, a very common infection in babies and toddlers, according to the NHS [3]. In roseola, it comes with a sudden high temperature and cold-like symptoms such as a sore throat, runny nose and cough, and these last 3 to 5 days before a pinkish-red rash appears on the chest, tummy and back [3]. You can normally look after your child at home and they should recover within a week [3].

Swelling of the eyelids can also be part of an allergic reaction, according to the SEUP [6]. In anaphylaxis, two or more organs are affected at once — most often skin, breathing, heart or gut — and the symptoms develop quickly [6]. Watch for swelling of the lips or ears, widespread intense redness, hives, trouble breathing, dizziness, loss of consciousness or vomiting [6]. If any of these appear, use the adrenaline auto-injector if one was prescribed and get medical help immediately [5][6].

q: what should I know about malaria symptoms in a child returning from Africa
text: Malaria is a potentially deadly infection spread by mosquito bites, and it is preventable and curable [1]. In a child returning from Africa, the first symptoms are usually fever, headache and chills, and they often appear 10 to 15 days after the bite of an infected mosquito [2]. Because early symptoms look like many other febrile illnesses, it is easy to mistake them for something else, so a test should be done as soon as possible [2]. Children under 5 are at higher risk of severe infection [1]. Severe signs include extreme tiredness, altered consciousness, seizures, difficulty breathing, dark or bloody urine, yellowing of the eyes and skin, and abnormal bleeding [2]. Anyone with severe symptoms needs emergency care quickly, and early treatment of a mild case can stop it getting worse [2].

q: why does my 3 year old have a temperature of 105 degree celsius
text:
105 °F = 40.6 °C.

A temperature of 105 °C is not possible — that is far above any body temperature. Fever means a body temperature above normal, usually around 37 °C (98.6 °F), and it is a sign the body is fighting an infection, according to MedlinePlus [1]. Most fevers are caused by infections, and fever itself is not an illness [1].

Check the thermometer and how you measured it: the armpit is the preferred place, and a rectal temperature is the most accurate, according to the AEPap [5]. If there are no warning signs, start with physical measures: remove extra clothing, give fluids, reduce activity, and a lukewarm bath if the child is comfortable [5].

Fever rarely goes above 40.5 °C (104.9 °F) and does not rise endlessly [5]. If the fever is very high, your health professional may recommend an over-the-counter medicine such as acetaminophen or ibuprofen [1]; paracetamol is the first choice in children, and ibuprofen is more effective when there is inflammation [4]. Children with fever should not take aspirin [1]. The dose depends on the child's weight.

18 lb = 8.2 kg.

A bump on the head from a fall is usually minor, because the skull is hard and protects the brain [2]. Most head injuries in children are mild and not dangerous [3].

q: she feels hot but the thermometer says 98.6
text:
A temperature of 98.6°F is normal, not a fever — a normal temperature is generally around 98.6°F or 37°C (98.6 °F), according to MedlinePlus [4]. A fever is a temperature of 38°C (100.4°F) or more [1][5].

If she feels hot but the thermometer reads normal, check how you took it: use a digital thermometer in the top of the armpit, keep the arm pressed to the side, and leave it in as long as the instructions say [1]. If she has just had a bath or been wrapped in a blanket, her temperature may read higher for a short time — wait a few minutes and try again [1].

If she does have a fever, the main goal is her comfort, not bringing the number down [2]. Make sure she drinks plenty of fluids, keep the room at a neutral temperature and ventilated, and avoid over-wrapping her [2]. It is normal for her to have less appetite — do not force her to eat [2]. Paracetamol or ibuprofen can be given at the dose your paediatrician recommends, every 6 to 8 hours [2]. Do not alternate them routinely every 3 to 4 hours unless she is uncomfortable before the 6 hours are up [2]. Do not bathe her in cold water or put wet cloths on her — it is unpleasant and does not work [2].

q: my child has a rash after having a fever, could it be from the fever
text:
If your child is under 3 months old, a fever needs a doctor the same day.

A rash that comes after a fever is often caused by a virus, and one common pattern is roseola (exantema súbito), according to the SEUP [2]. It usually affects babies 6 to 18 months old: 3 to 4 days of high fever with no other symptoms, then the fever drops and a faint, flat, widespread rash appears that is not itchy and lasts about 48 hours [2]. The diagnosis is made from this sequence of events [2].

There is no specific treatment for the rash itself; it fades on its own [2]. If your child seems uncomfortable from the fever, paracetamol is the first choice and ibuprofen is an option, with the dose based on your child's age and weight [5].

Get urgent help if your child is limp, barely responsive or very irritable, is breathing with difficulty, has spots that do not fade when you press them, or cannot keep down solids or fluids [1].

q: my toddler has very hard poop and cries when he goes
text:
Hard, painful poops are constipation: fewer than three bowel movements a week, with stool that is hard and dry and sometimes painful to pass, according to MedlinePlus [3]. It is common and in most cases lasts a short time and is not serious [3].

To help now: offer more liquids, preferably water, to soften the stool and make it easier to pass, and add more fibre — wholegrain cereals and bread, fruit and vegetables. Do not replace fruit with juice, because juice has little fibre, according to the SEUP [1]. Keep a regular routine and don't let him hold in the urge to go [1].

Most cases of constipation in children (95%) are not caused by any illness, and you should not give laxatives or enemas without asking your paediatrician [1]. It is not essential that a child poops every day — rhythm and consistency vary from person to person [1].

See your paediatrician if the constipation comes with bad abdominal pain, blood in the stool, or repeated vomiting with no solids or liquids kept down [1].

q: my 6 year old has a cough that is worse at night
text:
A cough that is worse at night is common in several childhood illnesses, and the cause is not always clear from the cough alone. In croup, a barking cough that sounds like a seal, a hoarse voice and noisy breathing are often worse at night and usually last about three to five days, according to MedlinePlus [6]. Asthma can also cause a persistent cough that is worse at night, along with wheezing or chest tightness [1][5]. Whooping cough causes coughing bouts that are worse at night and can last for weeks [4].

Most cases of viral croup are mild and can be treated at home [6]. If your child has a barking cough, ask for an urgent appointment with your doctor, because medicine may shorten the illness [3].

Get medical help right away if your child has severe coughing, serious breathing problems, or turns very pale or blue in the face, lips or fingernails [5]. If you are worried about your child's breathing, call your doctor right away [6].

q: can I give Nurofen as well

Ibuprofen should not be given if your child has continuous vomiting, and not under 3 months or under 5 kg [5]. The dose goes by weight, not age [5].

q: my 5 year old complains of stomach ache and won't eat anything
text:
A stomach ache with no appetite is common in children and often passes. Norovirus, a stomach bug, causes tummy pain and usually gets better in about 2 days, according to the NHS [4]. Constipation can also cause a stomach ache and feeling sick — it's likely if your child has not had a poo at least 3 times in the last week, or the poo is dry, hard or lumpy [6].

Offer small sips of fluid often, and let your child eat whatever they feel like when they're ready. Don't force them to eat — just take the food away without saying anything and try again another time [2]. If your child is active, gaining weight and seems well, they're getting enough to eat [3].

See your doctor if the stomach ache is severe, keeps coming back, or your child seems unwell in other ways.

q: my baby is 4 months and has a fever of 38
text:
A fever is usually the body's normal response to fighting an infection, and most children with a high temperature can be looked after at home, according to the NHS [1]. The temperature should come down over 1 to 4 days [1].

Keep breastfeeding as normal, and offer plenty of fluids [1]. Check on your baby regularly, including during the night, and keep them at home [1]. Do not undress them or sponge them down to cool them, and do not cover them in too many clothes or bedclothes [7]. If your baby is distressed or uncomfortable, the NHS says you can give either paracetamol or ibuprofen, checking the packaging or leaflet to make sure the medicine is suitable for your child, or speaking to a pharmacist or doctor if you are not sure [1]. Do not give ibuprofen to a baby under 3 months or under 5kg [7].

Get medical advice if you are worried about your child, or if the medicine is not helping [1].

q: my child got fever after vaccination yesterday
text:
If your child is under 3 months old, a fever needs a doctor the same day. For an older child, fever in the day or two after a vaccination is common and usually settles on its own.

Give plenty of fluids and dress them lightly. If they are uncomfortable, you can give paracetamol or ibuprofen, but the dose depends on their age and weight, so follow the dose your doctor or the leaflet gives. PediBot's dose calculator covers paracetamol and ibuprofen if you know their weight.

Vaccines are given at well-child visits according to the national vaccination schedule, which lets the body build protection before it meets serious diseases, according to MedlinePlus [3]. In India, the ages and doses follow India's national schedule.

See a doctor if the fever is high, lasts more than a couple of days, or your child is drowsy, breathing fast, or not drinking.

q: my 3 year old is coughing mostly at night, should I use a nebulizer
text:
A cough that is worse at night can be a sign of asthma in children, according to MedlinePlus [4]. Other signs include wheezing, chest tightness, and shortness of breath [4]. The NHS says asthma symptoms are often worse at night and early in the morning [6].

A nebulizer is not mentioned in these passages. For a child under four, do not give cough medicine [5]. Water can help ease a cough, whether they drink it or you add it to the air with a steamy shower or vaporizer [5].

See your doctor if your child has asthma symptoms, or if symptoms are waking them at night [6]. Get medical help right away if there is severe coughing, serious breathing problems, or turning very pale or blue in the face, lips or fingernails [4].

text: Your son needs fluids in small, frequent amounts, because the main risk from vomiting is dehydration, according to the SEUP [6]. The SEUP also says to seek urgent care if he vomits a lot and cannot keep down solids or liquids, or vomits even when he has taken nothing [4].

q: मेरे बच्चे को कल से दस्त हो रहे हैं और वह खाना नहीं खा रहा
text:
दस्त का इलाज मौखिक पुनर्जलीकरण घोल (ORS) से किया जाता है — यह साफ पानी, नमक और चीनी का घोल है, जो विश्व स्वास्थ्य संगठन के अनुसार आंतों में सोखा जाता है और मल के साथ निकले पानी और इलेक्ट्रोलाइट्स की भरपाई करता है [1]। साथ ही ज़िंक की गोलियाँ दस्त की अवधि को 25% तक घटाती हैं और मल की मात्रा में 30% तक कमी लाती हैं [1]।

खाना न खाने पर: दस्त के दौरान भी पोषक भोजन — जिसमें माँ का दूध भी शामिल है — देना जारी रखें, क्योंकि इससे कुपोषण और दस्त का चक्र टूटता है [1]।

स्वास्थ्य पेशेवर से सलाह लें, खासकर अगर दस्त लंबे समय तक बने रहें, मल में खून आए, या निर्जलीकरण के लक्षण दिखें [1]।

q: मेरे बच्चे को बुखार के साथ लाल दाने निकल आए हैं
text:
अगर बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा है, तो बुखार में उसी दिन डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है।

बुखार के साथ लाल दानों के कई कारण हो सकते हैं। खसरा 3 से 5 दिन बाद शुरू होता है — पहले सर्दी-जैसे लक्षण, फिर बालों की लाइन पर चपटे लाल दाने जो चेहरे से नीचे शरीर पर फैलते हैं, और दाने निकलते समय बुखार तेज़ हो सकता है, CDC के अनुसार [4]। चिकनपॉक्स में खुजली वाले दाने शरीर पर कहीं भी हो सकते हैं, साथ में तेज़ बुखार और बेचैनी, NHS के अनुसार [5]। हैंड, फुट और माउंट डिज़ीज़ में पहले गले में दर्द, तेज़ बुखार और खाने का मन न करना, फिर मुँह के छाले और हाथ-पैरों पर उभरे दाने होते हैं [3]।

इलाज के लिए: ठंडे तरल पदार्थ दें, खट्टे पेय जैसे फलों का रस न दें, दही जैसा नरम खाना दें, और तेज़ मसालेदार-नमकीन चीज़ें न दें [1]। दवा की खुराक बच्चे की उम्र और वज़न पर निर्भर करती है।

अगर मुँह के आसपास सूजन हो या साँस लेने में तकलीफ़ हो, तो तुरंत आपातकालीन नंबर पर कॉल करें [6]।

बच्चे की उम्र कितनी है? उम्र जानकर मैं जवाब और सटीक कर सकता हूँ।

q: मेरा 6 महीने का बच्चा दूध कम पी रहा है और पेशाब भी कम कर रहा है
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: पानी की कमी के लक्षण: आँखें धँसी, कम पेशाब, सूखा मुँह, लगातार उल्टी या 24 घंटे से ज़्यादा दस्त
text:
6 महीने के बच्चे में मुँह और जीभ का सूखना, बिना आँसू रोना, 3 घंटे या उससे ज़्यादा बिना गीला डायपर रहना और धँसी हुई आँखें निर्जलीकरण के संकेत हैं, MedlinePlus के अनुसार [2]। ऐसे में तुरंत डॉक्टरी मदद लेनी चाहिए, ख़ासकर अगर बेहोशी, भ्रम, तेज़ धड़कन या तेज़ साँस भी हो [2]।

जब तक मदद मिले, बच्चे को दूध पिलाते रहें — स्तनपान सामान्य रूप से और ज़रूरत पड़ने पर उससे भी ज़्यादा बार कराते रहें, SEUP के अनुसार [1]। दूध की मात्रा कम-कम और बार-बार दें ताकि उल्टी का ख़तरा कम हो [1]। दस्त हो तो ओरल रीहाइड्रेशन सॉल्यूशन (साफ़ पानी, चीनी और नमक का घोल) दें, WHO के अनुसार [4]। खेल-कूद वाले पेय और जूस न दें, क्योंकि उनमें चीनी ज़्यादा और इलेक्ट्रोलाइट असंतुलित होते हैं [1]।

q: मेरी बेटी बिस्तर से गिर गई और उसके बाद एक बार उल्टी हुई
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: सिर पर चोट के बाद उल्टी
text:
बच्चे के सिर पर चोट लगने के बाद उल्टी होना एक ऐसा लक्षण है जिस पर तुरंत ध्यान देने की ज़रूरत होती है। SEUP के मुताबिक़, अगर बच्चा उल्टी करता है या उसका व्यवहार चिंता की बात लगे, तो आपातकालीन विभाग में जाना चाहिए [1]। अगर गिरावट एक मीटर से ज़्यादा ऊँचाई से हुई हो, या बच्चा तीन महीने से छोटा हो, तो भी तुरंत डॉक्टर के पास जाना ज़रूरी है [1]।

जब तक मदद मिले, बच्चे को आराम से लिटाए रखें और उल्टी होने पर उसे करवट दिला दें ताकि उल्टी से दम न घुटे। होश बनाए रखने के लिए उसे बार-बार छोटे-छोटे घूँट पानी या ओआरएस दें, लेकिन ज़बरदस्ती न करें।

q: बच्चे को कब्ज है और पॉटी करते समय बहुत रोता है
text:
कब्ज़ के कारण बच्चे का रोना आम बात है — रोने के कई कारणों में से एक कब्ज़ भी है, ऐसा NHS कहता है [2]। अगर बच्चा लगातार रो रहा है और आप उसे चुप नहीं करा पा रहे हैं, या उसका रोना आम रोने जैसा नहीं लग रहा, तो यह बीमारी का संकेत हो सकता है [4]।

अगर बच्चा रोते समय मुट्ठियाँ भींचता है, चेहरा लाल कर लेता है, घुटने पेट की ओर खींचता है या पीठ मोड़ता है, तो यह कॉलिक हो सकता है — ऐसे में उसे दुलारकर शांत करने की कोशिश करें और रोना खुद शांत होने का इंतज़ार करें [1][2]।

अगर बच्चा बेचैन है, दूध पीना छोड़ देता है, उल्टी करता है, मल में खून आता है, या रोने के बीच सामान्य नहीं हो पाता, तो डॉक्टर से मिलें [6]।

q: मेरे बच्चे के हाथ पैर ठंडे हैं लेकिन शरीर गर्म है
text:
बुखार के दौरान हाथ-पैर ठंडे होना आम बात है: जब बुखार चढ़ रहा होता है तो बच्चे को ठंड लगती है, कभी-कभी कंपकंपी भी होती है, और खासकर हाथों और पैरों की त्वचा पर जाल जैसा लाल-नीला रंग दिख सकता है, जो SEUP के अनुसार सामान्य है [2]। जब बुखार उतरता है तो बच्चा पसीना-पसीना हो जाता है, लाल पड़ जाता है और उसे गर्मी लगती है [2]।

बुखार आमतौर पर शरीर के बचाव का संकेत है, ज़्यादातर मामलों में वायरल संक्रमण से होता है, और अपने आप में गंभीरता का मतलब नहीं है [4]। बुखार में बच्चे को बेचैनी लगना, भूख कम लगना, थकान या सिरदर्द होना भी सामान्य है [2]। ध्यान रखें कि बच्चा पर्याप्त तरल पिए, ताकि निर्जलीकरण न हो [1]। बुखार बहुत तेज़ हो तो डॉक्टर पैरासिटामोल या आइबुप्रोफेन जैसी दवा की सलाह दे सकते हैं; बच्चों को एस्पिरिन नहीं देनी चाहिए [1]। दवा की मात्रा बच्चे के वज़न पर निर्भर करती है — PediBot के डोज़ कैलकुलेटर से पैरासिटामोल और आइबुप्रोफेन की सही मात्रा देख सकते हैं।

q: मेरा बच्चा बहुत सुस्त है और ठीक से जाग नहीं रहा
banner: 🚨 अभी 112 पर कॉल करें या तुरंत इमरजेंसी ले जाएँ। | कारण: जवाब नहीं दे रहा; बहुत ज़्यादा सुस्ती या चिड़चिड़ापन
text:
बच्चे का सुस्त होना और ठीक से जाग न पाना निमोनिया की गंभीरता का संकेत है, विकासपीडिया के अनुसार [2]। ऐसे में तुरंत वैद्यकीय सहायता लेना चाहिए [2]।

जब तक मदद मिले, बच्चे को अपने पास रखें और उसका खान-पान चालू रखने की कोशिश करें, विकासपीडिया के अनुसार [2]। बुखार हो तो गुनगुने पानी में कपड़ा भिगोकर पूरा शरीर पोंछें, सिर्फ माथा नहीं [2]।

q: मेरे बच्चे ने आज बहुत कम पेशाब किया है
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: पानी की कमी के लक्षण: आँखें धँसी, कम पेशाब, सूखा मुँह, लगातार उल्टी या 24 घंटे से ज़्यादा दस्त
text: बच्चे का पेशाब कम आना निर्जलीकरण का संकेत हो सकता है, और ऐसे में बच्चे को तरल पदार्थ देना ज़रूरी है। निर्जलीकरण से बचने के लिए बच्चे को भरपूर पानी पिलाएँ, ताकि वह दिन में नियमित रूप से पेशाब करे [4]। अगर बच्चे को दस्त भी हो रहे हैं, तो SEUP के अनुसार उसे रोकने की ज़रूरत नहीं है — बच्चा लगभग सामान्य खाना खा सकता है, बस थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में और बार-बार दें ताकि उल्टी का ख़तरा कम हो; चिकनाई वाले खाने, मिठाइयों और जूस से बचें, और दस्त में स्पोर्ट्स ड्रिंक्स न दें क्योंकि उनमें चीनी ज़्यादा और इलेक्ट्रोलाइट्स बच्चे के लिए अनुपयुक्त होते हैं [1]। दूध और स्तनपान सामान्य रूप से जारी रखें, और अगर बच्चा माँगे तो और बार-बार दें [1]।

q: मेरी बेटी को तेज बुखार और बैंगनी जैसे दाग हो गए हैं
banner: 🚨 अभी 112 पर कॉल करें या तुरंत इमरजेंसी ले जाएँ। | कारण: दबाने पर न मिटने वाले दाने (सेप्सिस या मेनिन्जाइटिस का शक)
text:
अगर बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा है, तो बुखार में उसे उसी दिन डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है।

बुखार शरीर की संक्रमण से लड़ने की स्वाभाविक प्रतिक्रिया है, और आमतौर पर 1 से 4 दिनों में तापमान सामान्य हो जाता है [3]। त्वचा पर ऐसे दाग जो दबाने पर भी न मिटें, तेज बुखार के साथ, चिंता की बात है — SEUP के अनुसार ऐसे मामलों में तुरंत अस्पताल के आपातकालीन विभाग में जाना चाहिए [1]।

अभी के लिए: बच्चे को ज़्यादा कपड़ों या रजाई में न लपेटें, और उसे ठंडा करने के लिए कपड़े उतारकर स्पंज न करें [2]। बच्चे को पैरासिटामोल या आइबुप्रोफेन देने से पहले डॉक्टर या दवा के पर्चे की सलाह लें — खासकर अगर बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा है, 5 किलो से कम वजन का है, चिकनपॉक्स या अस्थमा है, या पानी की कमी है [2]। दवा की मात्रा बच्चे की उम्र और वजन पर निर्भर करती है, इसलिए वह डॉक्टर ही तय करेंगे।

अगर बच्चा सुस्त हो, ठीक से जाग न पाए, सांस लेने में तकलीफ हो, या खाना-पीना बंद कर दे, तो तुरंत डॉक्टर से मिलें [1][2]।

q: mere 3 saal ke bacche ko bukhar 102 hai, paracetamol kitna du
text: Paracetamol bukhar aur takleef mein madad karta hai, aur aap ise dukaan ya pharmacy se le sakte hain [4]. AEPap ke mutabiq, paracetamol 4-6 ghante ke antar par diya ja sakta hai, aur din mein paanch se zyada baar nahi [3]. Dawa ki matra bachche ke wazan ke hisaab se tay hoti hai, umar se nahi [3]. PediBot ka dose calculator paracetamol ke liye maujood hai, jahan aap sahi matra nikaal sakte hain [3]. Agar bachche ko 3-4 ghante baad bhi bukhar aur takleef mein aaram nahi milta, to agla antitérmico badalna theek hai [5]. Agar aapne packet ya leaflet se zyada paracetamol de diya hai, to turant medical advice lein [7].

q: mera baby raat ko bahut khans raha hai
text:
Raat ko khansi bachchon mein asthma ka ek lakshan ho sakti hai, aur yeh khaas taur par raat mein ya subah jaldi hoti hai [1]. SEUP ke mutabiq bachchon mein khansi (kabhi raat ko), saans lene mein takleef aur ghabrahat ho sakti hai [3].

Ghar par aaram karayein, khoob saara taraL daayein, aur saaf humidifier ya thande bhaap wala vaporizer istemal karein [6]. SEUP ke mutabiq khansi ke sharbat, mucolytics, steroids, antibiotics aur respiratory physiotherapy faaydemand nahi hain [2]. Kisi bhi dawa se pehle apne doctor se poochein [6].

Agar saans lene mein sakht takleef ho, seene mein dhadkan tez ho, honton ya chehre par neela rang dikhe, ya bachcha doodh peena chhod de, to turant medical madad lein [1][3][5].

q: mere bete ke pairon par lal dane hain aur khujli ho rahi hai
text:
Aapke bete ke pairon par lal dane aur khujli heat rash (prickly heat) ke lakshan ho sakte hain — chhote, ubhre hue dane aur khujli wali feeling iske aam lakshan hain, aur yeh brown ya kaali skin par grey ya safed bhi dikh sakta hai [6].

Ghar par sabse zaroori hai skin ko thanda rakhna taaki pasina aakar rash ko na chidhaye: dheele cotton kapde pehnao, halki rajai use karo, thande paani se nahi, halke thande paani se nahi — thande snan karwao, aur paani zyada pilao [6]. Khujli ke liye thandi cheez jaise geele kapde ya ice pack (toliya mein lipti hui) 20 minute tak lagao, aur rash ko kharochne ke bajaye thap-thap karo [6]. Perfumed shower gel ya cream mat lagao [6].

Agar aap sure nahi hain ki yeh heat rash hai, to doosre rashes bhi dekh lo [6].
sources: [6] NHS — "Heat rash (prickly heat)" (2024), section "Heat rash (prickly heat)", p. 1 — ht

q: mera bachcha bed se gir gaya aur ek baar ulti ki
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: सिर पर चोट के बाद उल्टी
text:
Mera bachcha bed se gir gaya aur ek baar ulti ki — SEUP ke mutabiq sirf ek baar ulti hona apne aap koi khatre ki baat nahi hai, lekin sar par chot ke baad ulti ko halka nahi samajhna chahiye [1].

Abhi kya karein: bachche ko aaram se rakhein, hilayein ya jhatka na dein, aur kuch bhi khilane-pilane se pehle doctor se poochhein [1]. Agar bachcha sust, neend mein, ya uthane par theek se jawab na de, to turant madad lein [1].

Doctor se milna zaroori hai agar bachcha 3 mahine se chhota hai, ya girne ki unchai ek meter se zyada thi [1]. SEUP ke mutabiq doctor zaroori jaanch karenge aur zarurat pade to kuch test bhi kar sakte hain, halanki zyadatar mamlon mein iski zarurat nahi padti [1].

Agar ulti verd (green) ho, khoon ho, ya coffee ke til jaisi dikhe, ya bachche ko tez sar dard ya pet dard ho, to bina der kiye doctor ke paas jaayein [3].

q: mere bacche ko kabz hai aur potty karte waqt rota hai
text:
Bacche ka kabz hona unka rehna aam baat hai, lekin potty karte waqt rona takleef ki nishani hai. NHS ke mutabiq, agar aapko samajh nahi aa raha ki kya galat hai, to apne doctor se baat karein ya swasthya karyakarta se poochein [3].

Ghar par yeh karein: bacche ko paani ya juice chhote-chhote ghoont mein zyada baar dein, aur pet par halke haath se halka dabaav dein. Agar bacche ko doodh pilate hain to maa ka doodh ya formula jaari rakhein.

NHS ke mutabiq, agar bacche ka rona lagatar ho aur aap use chup nahi kara sakte, ya rona uske normal rone jaisa na lage, to yeh bimaari ka sanket ho sakta hai — aise mein turant doctor se milein [7]. Agar bacche ko tez bukhar ho, doodh peena band kar de, ya 8 ghante se peshaab na aaya ho, to bhi doctor se milein [7].
sources: [3] NHS — "Colic" (2022), section "Symptoms of colic", p. 1 — https://www.nhs.uk/condition

q: mere bete ko saans lene mein dikkat lag rahi hai
banner: 🚨 अभी 112 पर कॉल करें या तुरंत इमरजेंसी ले जाएँ। | कारण: साँस लेने में गंभीर दिक्कत (पसलियाँ दिखना, बहुत तेज़ साँस, साँस रुकना, नीलापन)
text:
Saans lene mein dikkat kai cheezon se ho sakti hai, jaise RSV, croup ya bronchiolitis, aur inme shuruaat mein zukaam jaise halke lakshan hote hain jo kuch dino mein badh sakte hain [2][4]. Croup mein bhaunkne jaisi khaansi, awaaz baithna aur saans lete waqt tez, karkash awaaz ho sakti hai [3]. Bronchiolitis mein bachcha tez saans leta hai, dudh peena mushkil ho jata hai aur wheezing ya crackling awaaz aati hai [5].

Agar bachche ko saans lene mein takleef ho, turant madad lene ki koshish karein [5]. Kuch bachche RSV se zyada gambhir roop se beemar ho sakte hain, isliye unhe aspatal bheja ja sakta hai [3].

Dhyan rakhein: tez saans, pasliyan andar khinchana, saans mein rukawat, ya hothon ka neela ya grey hona gambhir lakshan hain [5].

[3] NHS — "Croup" (2025), section "Symptoms of croup", p. 1 — https://www.nhs.uk/condition
[4] Gouvernement du Canada — "Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV): Symptoms and treatment",
[5] NHS — "Bronchiolitis" (2026), section "Symptoms of bronchiolitis", p. 1 — https://www.

q: mera bachcha bahut tez saans le raha hai
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: साँस की दिक्कत: तेज़ साँस, सीटी जैसी आवाज़, पसलियाँ दिखना
text:
तेज़ साँस लेना शिशुओं और छोटे बच्चों में ब्रोंकियोलाइटिस या RSV जैसी साँस की बीमारी का लक्षण हो सकता है — NHS के अनुसार ब्रोंकियोलाइटिस में बच्चा तेज़ साँस लेता है, उसे खाने-पीने में दिक्कत होती है और साँस में घरघराहट या चटकने की आवाज़ आती है [3]। CDC के अनुसार RSV शुरू में हल्का लग सकता है, पर कुछ दिनों में गंभीर हो सकता है; शुरुआती लक्षणों में नाक बहना, कम खाना-पीना और खाँसी शामिल हैं, जो आगे चलकर घरघराहट या साँस लेने में कठिनाई बन सकती है [2]।

अभी बच्चे को गोद में सीधा और आराम से रखें, और थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में बार-बार दूध या तरल दें ताकि पानी की कमी न हो [3]। WHO के अनुसार पाँच साल से छोटे बच्चों में खाँसी या साँस लेने में तकलीफ के साथ तेज़ साँस चलना (ताकीपनिया) या पसलियों के नीचे धँसाव निमोनिया का संकेत हो सकता है [6]।

q: my 2 year old has bad cough at night not sleeping
text:
A cough that is worse at night and stops your child sleeping is common with whooping cough: the coughing bouts last a few minutes, are worse at night, and can go on for several weeks [2]. The cough may come in fits, with vomiting afterwards and exhaustion, and these fits often happen more at night [3].

Keep the room cool and give small sips of fluid often. If your child's lips, tongue, face or skin turn blue or grey, or they are finding it hard to breathe, get emergency help at once [4]. Ask for an urgent appointment with your doctor if the cough is very bad and getting worse [4].

q: my 5 year old baby has red pimples on full body
text:
A rash that spreads over the whole body can be caused by more than one illness, and the sources describe several. Measles causes a red, blotchy rash that usually starts on the head and moves down the body, along with fever, cough, runny nose and red, watery eyes [2]. Chickenpox causes an itchy rash that turns into fluid-filled blisters and then scabs, often starting on the face, chest and back before spreading [5].

There is no treatment for measles itself, but the MMR vaccine prevents it [2]. For chickenpox, calamine lotion and oatmeal baths can help with the itching, and acetaminophen can help with fever — do not give aspirin, because with chickenpox it can cause Reye's syndrome [5].

Because a whole-body rash in a young child can be serious, have your child seen by your doctor so the cause can be checked.

q: my 6 year old child is not eating anything from 2 days
text:
It's natural to worry if your child refuses to eat, and it's normal for children to refuse food sometimes, according to the NHS [5]. What matters more is what they eat over a week rather than in a single day, and if your child is active, gaining weight and seems well, they're likely getting enough [5].

Keep offering a variety of foods and go back to foods they refused before, as tastes change [5]. Give small portions, praise them for eating even a little, and don't force or leave meals until they're too hungry or tired [2]. Offer no more than 2 healthy snacks a day between meals [2].

See your doctor if your child refuses to eat or drink, or has persistent or intense tummy pain, according to the SEUP [1].

q: my 6 month old baby has congested chest and making whistling noise
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Breathing difficulty: fast breathing, wheezing, ribs pulling in
text:
A whistling or wheezing noise with a congested chest in a 6-month-old is often caused by a viral chest infection, and in babies under 2 the most common is bronchiolitis, according to the SEUP [4]. It usually starts like a normal cold with cough and mucus, and breathing difficulty can appear after 2 to 4 days [6].

Keep feeding them and offer fluids often, since feeding is one of the things that gets harder [6]. Keep them sleeping propped up semi-upright [5]. There is no medicine that cures bronchiolitis; most cases improve in about 2 weeks, though the cough can last longer [5].

While you get help, watch their breathing, how well they feed, their colour and general state, and any fever [5]. Wheezing is more common with viral infections, and fast breathing or pulling in of the lower ribs are the signs that mean pneumonia [7].

बुखार छोटे बच्चों में बहुत आम है और आमतौर पर 1 से 4 दिन में अपने आप उतर जाता है [1]। 38°C या उससे ज़्यादा तापमान बुखार माना जाता है [1]।

अभी यह करें: बच्चे को खूब तरल दें — अगर स्तनपान कराती हैं तो सामान्य रूप से जारी रखें; निर्जलीकरण के संकेत देखें; भूख लगे तो खाना दें; रात में भी नियमित रूप से जाँचते रहें; बच्चे को घर पर रखें [3]। अगर बच्चा बेचैन या असहज लगे तो पैरासिटामोल या आइबुप्रोफेन दें — पैकेट या पर्ची देखकर पक्का करें कि दवा इस उम्र के लिए ठीक है, या फार्मासिस्ट या डॉक्टर से पूछें [3]। 6 महीने के बच्चे को एस्पिरिन न दें [2]। बच्चे को कपड़े उतारकर या स्पंज करके ठंडा करने की कोशिश न करें, और ज़्यादा कपड़ों या रज़ाइयों में न लपेटें [2]।

अगर बच्चा 3 से 6 महीने का है और तापमान 39°C या ज़्यादा है, या बुखार के साथ दाने जैसे बीमारी के और संकेत हैं, तो तुरंत मदद लें [2]।

q: क्या बुखार उतारने के लिए बच्चे को नहला सकती हूँ? (उम्र: 6 महीने) (वज़न: 5 किलो)
text:
नहीं, बुखार उतारने के लिए बच्चे को नहलाना या स्पंज करना नहीं चाहिए — तेज़ बुखार शरीर की संक्रमण से लड़ने की स्वाभाविक और स्वस्थ प्रतिक्रिया है, ऐसा NHS कहता है [7]। बच्चे को ज़्यादा कपड़ों या रज़ाई में न लपेटें [7]।

बुखार उतारने के लिए गुनगुने पानी में कपड़ा भिगोकर पूरा शरीर पोंछ लें, सिर्फ माथा नहीं, और बच्चे का खाना-पीना चालू रखें, ऐसा विकासपीडिया बताता है [3]। 6 महीने के बच्चे को पैरासिटामोल दी जा सकती है, पर 2 महीने से छोटे बच्चे को नहीं [7]। 5 किलो वज़न वाले बच्चे को इबुप्रोफेन न दें [7]। दवा की मात्रा बच्चे के वज़न पर निर्भर करती है।

अगर बच्चा खाने-पीने या स्तनपान से मना करे, सुस्त हो जाए, साँस लेते समय पसलियाँ अंदर खिंचें, या त्वचा, होंठ या नाखून नीले दिखें, तो तुरंत डॉक्टर से मिलें [3]।

q: 3 साल के बच्चे को सूखी खांसी और छाती से सीटी की आवाज आ रही है
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: साँस की दिक्कत: तेज़ साँस, सीटी जैसी आवाज़, पसलियाँ दिखना
text:
सूखी खांसी और सांस लेते समय सीटी जैसी आवाज़ बच्चों में श्वसन संक्रमण के कारण हो सकती है — प्रीस्कूल उम्र के बच्चों में सीटी की आवाज़ का मुख्य कारण वायरल श्वसन संक्रमण होता है, SEUP के अनुसार [2]। NHS के अनुसार क्रूप में भौंकने जैसी खांसी, आवाज़ बैठना और सांस लेते समय तेज़ रसने वाली आवाज़ होती है, और ये लक्षण अक्सर रात में ज़्यादा बिगड़ते हैं [3]।

अभी बच्चे को शांत रखें और सीधा बैठाएँ, ताकि सांस लेना आसान हो। SEUP के अनुसार सीटी की आवाज़ ब्रोन्कोडाइलेटर दवाओं (जैसे साल्बुटामोल) से सुधरती है, पर यह दवा डॉक्टर के बताए अनुसार ही दी जाती है [2]। बच्चे को खूब तरल पदार्थ छोटे-छोटे घूँट में दें और आराम करने दें [6]।

NHS के अनुसार अगर आपको लगता है कि बच्चे को क्रूप हो सकता है, तो तुरंत डॉक्टर से मिलें, क्योंकि दवा बीमारी को छोटा कर सकती है [3]।

q: मेरे 5 साल के बच्चे के शरीर पर लाल दाने हो गए हैं और खुजली है
text:
लाल दाने और खुजली कई चीज़ों से हो सकते हैं। बहुत खुजली वाले उभरे दाने उन नन्हें कीड़ों से हो सकते हैं जो त्वचा में घुस जाते हैं (स्केबीज़), और उंगलियों के बीच एक सिरे पर बिंदु वाली उभरी लकीरें दिख सकती हैं [4]। स्केबीज़ का इलाज आमतौर पर घर पर ही किया जा सकता है [4]।

अगर यह घमौरी है, तो त्वचा को ठंडा रखें: ढीले सूती कपड़े पहनाएँ, हल्का बिस्तर लगाएँ, ठंडे पानी से नहलाएँ और खूब तरल पदार्थ पिलाएँ [6]। खुजली शांत करने के लिए ठंडी चीज़ (गीला कपड़ा या तौलिये में लपेटी आइस पैक) 20 मिनट तक लगाएँ, और खुजाने की जगह दानों को थपथपाएँ [6]। सुगंधित शॉवर जेल या क्रीम न लगाएँ [6]।

अगर बच्चा 2 साल से छोटा हो या घर में किसी और को भी स्केबीज़ हो, त्वचा में संक्रमण लगे, या फार्मेसी का इलाज पूरा होने के 2 से 4 हफ्ते बाद भी खुजली बनी रहे, तो डॉक्टर को दिखाएँ [1]।

q: क्या एमएमआर वैक्सीन बच्चे के लिए सुरक्षित है
text:
एमएमआर वैक्सीन के बारे में nidirect कहता है कि बच्चों को अलग-अलग उम्र में टीके लगते हैं और नियमित टीकाकरण आठ सप्ताह की उम्र से शुरू होता है [1]। वैक्सीन के समय और कौन-सा टीका कब लगेगा, यह भारत के राष्ट्रीय टीकाकरण कार्यक्रम के अनुसार तय होता है [1]।

विकासपीडिया के अनुसार, लगभग सभी वैक्सीन्स के थोड़े-बहुत दुष्प्रभाव हो सकते हैं, जो मामूली से गंभीर तक हो सकते हैं, फिर भी ये सारे टीके काफी सुरक्षित हैं और मामूली दुष्प्रभावों का इलाज आसानी से हो जाता है [6]। दुष्प्रभाव होना यह संकेत है कि वैक्सीन अपना असर दिखा रही है [6]।

nidirect यह भी कहता है कि टीके सुरक्षित और प्रभावी हैं तथा जान बचा सकते हैं, और समय पर लगना सबसे अच्छी सुरक्षा देता है [4]। अगर कोई टीका छूट जाए, तो अपने डॉक्टर से संपर्क करें [4]।

q: 3 saal ke bacche ko raat ko bahut khansi aati hai
text:
3 saal ke bacche mein raat ki khansi aam taur par laringitis (croup) ki wajah se ho sakti hai, jismein bachche raat bhar kaafi khaanste hain aur theek se so nahi paate [6]. SEUP ke mutabik zyadatar laringitis halki hoti hai aur kuch dinon mein theek ho jaati hai, lekin ek hafte tak bhi reh sakti hai [6].

Ghar par: agar bukhar ho to bacche ko liquids pilaiye aur usual bukhar ki dawa dijiye [6]. Aaram karne dein [6].

NHS/SEUP ke mutabik in par dhyan rakhein: bacche ki saans lene ki koshish — kabhi kabhi laringe ki sujan se hawa andar jaane mein dikkat hoti hai; bacche ka rang aur uski general halat [6]. Agar saans lene mein dikkat badhe, ya baccha sust ya bahut bechain ho, ya rang neela ya peela lage, to turant doctor se milna chahiye [7].

q: mera 8 month ka baby bed se gir gaya aur ro raha hai
text: Sar mein chot lagne par aam taur par sar dard, chakkar aana, ulti aur neend aana jaise lakshan dikh sakte hain, SEUP ke mutabik [1]. Ghar par aaram karaiye: 24 se 48 ghante tak sharirik aur mansik aaram zaroori hai, jitna chot gehri ho utna zyada [2]. Is dauran khel-kood aur mobile, tablet ya video game bilkul na karaiye [2]. Khana pehle jaisa hi chalega, koi khaas parhez nahi [6]. Agar sar dard ho to doctor ke bataye dose mein paracetamol ya ibuprofen diya ja sakta hai [6]. Sone de sakte hain, lekin gehri chot mein har 4 ghante jagana chahiye [6]. In lakshanon par turant doctor ke paas jaiye: tez ya badhta sar dard, baar-baar ulti, confusion, bahut chidchidapan ya jagane par mushkil se uthna, bolne ya chalne mein dikkat, naak ya kaan se khoon ya saaf paani [2][5].

q: 5 saal ke child ko body pe red rashes ho gaye hain
text:
5 saal ke bachche ki body par red rashes ke liye, WHO ke mutabik khaas taur par chhote bachchon mein sarna (scabies) se hone wali eruption palms, soles aur scalp par zyada hoti hai, aur ismein raat ko tez khujli hoti hai [2]. Agar rashes ke saath tez bukhar, khaansi, naak behna aur aankhein laal hon, to WHO ke mutabik yeh khasra (measles) ho sakta hai, jismein daane pehle chehre aur gale se shuru hokar teen din mein poore sharir par phail jaate hain [3].

Kya karein: WHO ke mutabik sarna ka ilaaj cream ya dawa se hota hai, isliye bachche ko doctor dikhayein taaki sahi ilaaj mile [5]. Khujli aur daane kam karne ke liye bachche ke nakhun chhote rakhein taaki khujlane se skin par infection na ho [2].

Turant madad lein agar bachche ke hoth, munh, gala ya jeebh soojh jaaye, saans lene mein dikkat ho, ya bachcha sust, behosh ya jawab na de — yeh gambhir allergic reaction ke signs hain [7].

q: kya polio ki drop dena zaroori hai
text: Polio ki drop dena zaroori hai. WHO kehta hai ki difteria se bachne ka sabse asardar tareeka tikakaran hai, aur difteria ki vaccine aksar polio ki inactivated vaccine ke saath mil kar di jaati hai [6]. Spain ke Ministry of Sanidad ke calendar ke mutabik polio (VPI) vaccine 2, 4 aur 11 mahine ki umar mein di jaati hai, aur 6 saal ki umar par booster bhi [3]. CAV-AEP kehta hai ki vulnerable ya migrant parivaron ke bachchon mein bhi vaccine ka calendar nahi badalta, bas use samay par pura karne par zor diya jaata hai [1]. Apne bachche ke liye sahi umar aur schedule ke baare mein apne doctor se poochhein.

q: my baby has diarrhea after we came back from a trip
text:
Diarrhoea after travel is usually an infection of the gut, and the most important thing is to keep your baby hydrated, according to the WHO [1]. Give oral rehydration salts (ORS) — a mixture of clean water, salt and sugar — which replace the water and electrolytes lost in the stools [1]. Zinc supplements are also a key treatment: they reduce how long the diarrhoea lasts by 25% and cut stool volume by 30% [1]. Keep giving nutrient-rich foods, including breast milk, during the episode [1].

Get help from a health professional if the diarrhoea is persistent, if there is blood in the stool, or if there are signs of dehydration [1]. Signs of dehydration include crying without tears, passing little urine, sunken eyes, marked irritability or drowsiness, and being unable to drink as fast as the fluid is lost [3]. Do not use homemade solutions or commercial soft drinks to replace the losses [3].

q: my child has been in the sun and now feels dizzy
text:
Heat illness happens when the body can't cool itself, and being out in the sun too long is one of the causes, according to the SEUP [1]. Dizziness is one of the symptoms to watch for [1].

Move your child to a cool, shady place and take off extra clothing. Put cool wet cloths on the forehead, neck and armpits, offer cool water in small sips, and use a fan to help bring the temperature down [6]. Do not give fever medicines for heat illness — physical cooling measures are used instead, according to the AEPap [5].

Go to the emergency department if there is loss of consciousness or seizures, confusion or trouble speaking or moving, or persistent vomiting with inability to drink [7].

q: my child has loose motions since morning what should I give
text: Give your child an oral rehydration solution to replace the fluids and electrolytes they are losing, according to MedlinePlus [1]. Oral rehydration solution is a mix of clean water, salt and sugar, and it is absorbed in the small intestine [3]. Do not use homemade solutions or fizzy drinks to replace the losses from gastroenteritis, and do not give medicines to stop the diarrhoea or vomiting without asking your paediatrician, according to the SEUP [4]. Keep offering food: no fasting is needed, just smaller amounts more often, and avoid fatty foods, sweets and juices — sports drinks should also be avoided because they have too much sugar for a child with diarrhoea [6]. Contact a provider right away if your child has a change in mental state such as irritability or lack of energy, diarrhoea lasting more than a day, any fever in an infant, frequent loose stools, vomiting often, severe belly pain, signs of dehydration such as thirst, dry mouth, urinating less than usual or no wet nappies for 3 hours or more, or stools that are black and tarry or contain blood or pus [2].

q: is MMR vaccine safe for my daughter
text:
The MMR vaccine is safe and effective, according to the NHS. Protection starts within 2 weeks of having it, and after 2 doses around 99% of people are protected against measles and rubella and around 88% against mumps [2]. If someone does get mumps after being vaccinated, the symptoms are usually much milder [2].

The ages for each dose follow India's national immunisation schedule, so check your daughter's due dates with your doctor.

If you have any questions about your daughter's vaccines, your doctor can go through them with you.

q: my 6 month old has started solids, can I give banana
text: Yes, you can give banana. Soft fruit such as banana is listed as a good finger food, according to the NHS [5]. Cut it into pieces big enough for your baby to hold in their fist with a bit sticking out — about the size of your own finger [5]. Start with finger foods that break up easily in the mouth, and avoid hard foods like raw apple or whole nuts, to reduce the risk of choking [5]. Offer finger foods at each meal to help them learn to self-feed [5]. At first, how much they eat matters less than getting used to eating; they still get most of their energy and nutrients from breast milk or first infant formula [3].

q: my 5 year old has stomach pain and constipation
text:
Constipation is the likely cause: a child may have a stomach ache and feel bloated or sick when they have not pooed at least 3 times in the last week, or when the poo is large, small, dry, hard or lumpy, according to the NHS [1]. Abdominal pain in children is common and most often harmless and settles on its own, and constipation is one of its usual causes, according to the SEUP [2].

For a 5 year old, give more fluids, preferably water, to soften the poo and make it easier to pass, and more meals with fibre — wholegrain cereals and bread, fruit and vegetables. Do not replace fruit with juice, as juice has little fibre [3]. Keep a regular routine and do not let them hold in the urge to go to the toilet [3].

See a doctor if the pain is severe, if they are very down and complaining a lot, if there is blood in the poo, or if they vomit many times and cannot keep down solids or liquids [3]. Do not give laxatives or enemas without asking your paediatrician [3].

q: my child has been scratching small bumps on his body
text:
Small, itchy raised spots like these are often heat rash, according to the NHS. Heat rash is uncomfortable but usually harmless and usually gets better on its own after a few days [4].

To help now: keep the skin cool so he does not sweat and irritate the rash. Loose cotton clothing, lightweight bedding, cool baths or showers, and plenty of fluids to avoid dehydration [4]. To calm the itching, apply something cold — a damp cloth or an ice pack wrapped in a tea towel — for up to 20 minutes, and pat or tap the rash instead of scratching it. Do not use perfumed shower gels or creams [4].

If the spots are more like raised, puffy patches, that is hives, and a pharmacist can advise about antihistamine treatment — though it may not be suitable for young children [7].

See your doctor if the rash is bad, does not go away, or comes with other symptoms [5].

q: my daughter has fever after coming back from a trip
text:
If your child is under 3 months old, a fever needs a doctor the same day. For an older child: a high temperature is very common in young children, and it usually returns to normal within 1 to 4 days, according to the NHS [1]. Fever is not an illness itself — it is usually a sign the body is fighting an infection, and most fevers are caused by infections, according to MedlinePlus [3].

Check the temperature with a digital thermometer in the armpit, and if they have just had a bath or been wrapped up, wait a few minutes and try again [1]. Keep them drinking enough fluids to prevent dehydration [3]. Do not undress them or sponge them down, and do not cover them in too many clothes or bedclothes [7]. Do not give aspirin to a child under 16 [7].

Because you were travelling, contact your doctor when you return home if your child was sick with a fever while travelling, according to MedlinePlus [6].

q: what food to give 6 month baby for first time
text: Around 6 months, start with small amounts of food — just a few pieces or teaspoons — before their usual milk feed, when your baby is not too tired and you are not rushed, according to the NHS [1]. Offer different foods and keep offering even ones they reject; it can take 10 tries or more before a baby accepts a new food or texture [1]. Breast milk or first infant formula stays their main drink, and you can offer sips of water with meals from an open or free-flow cup [1]. The WHO says to begin with small amounts at 6 months and increase gradually, moving to 2–3 meals a day between 6 and 8 months, and to keep breastfeeding on demand [3].

q: my 4 year old has severe cough and catarrh
text:
A severe cough with catarrh (a runny nose) can be the first phase of whooping cough, which usually lasts 1 to 2 weeks and looks like a cold, with fever, runny nose, red watery eyes and a mild or occasional cough and sneezing, according to the Government of Canada [4]. The cough then becomes more severe, with uncontrollable coughing fits that can make it hard to breathe [4].

Treatment depends on your child's age and how long they have had the infection, according to the NHS [6]. If whooping cough is diagnosed within 3 weeks of the cough starting, antibiotics are given to help stop it spreading to others, though they may not reduce symptoms [6]. Keep taking the antibiotics until the course is finished, even if your child feels better [6].

Whooping cough is less severe in older children, but the coughing can cause sore ribs, hernia, middle ear infections or leaking pee when coughing [2].

q: my 5 year old fell down and hurt his leg leg is swollen
text:
A swollen leg after a fall can be a sprain or strain, an injury to the muscles and ligaments that is usually treated at home, according to the NHS [3]. The injured area being swollen or bruised, with pain, tenderness or weakness, and not being able to put weight on it or use it normally, are signs of this [3].

What to do now: rest the leg, and if it is painful or swollen, raise it and put an ice pack or a bag of frozen peas wrapped in a cloth on the injury for up to 20 minutes every 2 to 3 hours. If needed, give paracetamol or ibuprofen for the pain — the dose depends on your child's weight, and PediBot's dose calculator can work it out for these two medicines.

Get help if your child cannot put any weight on the leg, the leg looks crooked or there is numbness, or the pain and swelling get worse rather than better [3].

q: my 18 month old is refusing food and crying when chewing
text:
It's common for toddlers to refuse food sometimes, and it's normal for them to refuse to eat or even taste new foods, according to the NHS [3]. If your child is active, gaining weight and seems well, they're getting enough to eat [3].

Give small portions and praise them for eating, even a little [6]. If they reject food, don't force them — take it away without saying anything and try again another time [6]. Offer the same food as the rest of the family, without added salt, and eat with them so they can copy you [6]. Keep offering a variety of foods; it may take many attempts before they accept some [3]. Two healthy snacks a day between meals is plenty [6].

Crying when chewing is not covered by these pages, so ask your doctor to check your child's mouth and teeth.

q: my baby is not passing urine as much as usual
text:
A baby who is passing less urine than usual may be dehydrated, and babies are among those most likely to become dehydrated [2]. Signs of dehydration in a baby include thirst, a dry mouth, or not wetting their nappies for 3 hours or more and no tears when crying, according to MedlinePlus [6].

Keep offering fluids. If your baby is finding it hard to keep fluids down, try small sips of water or pieces of ice to suck [3]. Avoid sugary and caffeinated drinks [3].

See a doctor as soon as possible if your baby has any signs of dehydration, such as passing less urine than usual or not wetting their nappies for 3 hours or more [6].

q: my baby fell from the bed and seems normal now
text:
A knock on the head from a fall is a common reason for a head injury, and most head injuries are mild and not dangerous, according to the SEUP [1][2]. It is important to watch your child for the first 24 hours after the knock to spot signs of seriousness [2].

Let them rest physically and mentally for 24 to 48 hours, depending on how hard the knock was, with no sport and no screens, then return to normal activities gradually [5]. Watch at home for a severe or worsening headache that does not improve with the usual paracetamol or ibuprofen, repeated vomiting, confusion or disorientation, and in very small children irritability or being hard to wake [5].

Go to the emergency department if your child has any of those symptoms, if their behaviour worries you, if they are under three months old, or if the fall was from more than one metre [4].

There is no medicine that cures bronchiolitis; most cases improve over about 2 weeks, though the cough can last longer [7]. If you are worried about your child's breathing, call your healthcare provider right away, according to MedlinePlus [5].

q: my 3 year old has fever 102, can I give Calpol
text:
102 °F = 38.9 °C.

Yes, paracetamol (Calpol) can help when your child is distressed or uncomfortable from a high temperature, according to the NHS [3]. It is a common children's painkiller that relieves pain and high temperature [4].

The main goal is your child's comfort, not bringing the fever down to normal, according to the SEUP [2]. Make sure they drink plenty of fluids and are not over-wrapped, and do not force them to eat [2]. Paracetamol and ibuprofen both work, and are given at the dose your paediatrician recommends, every 6 to 8 hours [2]. Do not routinely alternate the two every 3 to 4 hours unless your child is uncomfortable before the 6 hours are up [2]. Do not bathe them in cold water or use wet cloths — it is unpleasant and does not work [2]. Children with fever should not take aspirin [1].

q: can I give ORS to my 1 year old after diarrhea
text: Yes — oral rehydration salts (ORS) are one of the main treatments for diarrhoea, according to the WHO [1]. ORS is a mixture of clean water, salt and sugar that is absorbed in the small intestine and replaces the water and electrolytes lost in the stools [1]. Zinc supplements are also a key treatment: they reduce how long the diarrhoea lasts by 25% and cut stool volume by 30% [1]. Keep giving nutrient-rich foods, including breast milk, during the episode [1]. Do not use homemade solutions or commercial soft drinks to replace the losses [3]. See a health professional for persistent diarrhoea, blood in the stool, or signs of dehydration [1].

text:
Un sarpullido rojo que pica en las piernas puede ser una urticaria: ronchas o habones rojos y elevados que pican mucho, y que van apareciendo en unas zonas mientras desaparecen de otras, según la SEUP [3]. En la infancia, la mayoría de las urticarias las causa una infección, no una alergia [3].

También puede tratarse de una reacción a picaduras de insectos, que da lesiones muy pruriginosas y suele afectar las zonas descubiertas como brazos y piernas, según Ecimed [6]. Evita que se rasque, porque el rascado puede infectar las lesiones [6].

Si además aparecen hinchazón de manos, pies, codos o cara, o dificultad para respirar o tragar, hay que buscar atención médica de inmediato [3].
